after: Under ⚙ → App, language packs & backup you download the languages you need. Each pack contains all the translations, conjugations, grammar and menus for that language.

Once installed as an app, Fraxx opens with a compact home page: a search field, tiles for all sections, your quiz progress and the sections you opened most recently. For the full introduction, tap “What is Fraxx?” there.
Everything that's installed works without internet: on a plane, abroad without mobile data, or in a dead zone.
Reading aloud uses your device's voices. On Mac and Windows, Chrome usually sounds the most natural. You can install more voices in your device's language settings.
Your stars, learning progress and settings are stored on your device. Under ⚙ → App, language packs & backup you can download a backup and restore it whenever you need to.
When there's a new version, a dot appears on the ⚙. There you can see what's new and decide when to update.
appcap: App, language packs & backup: add or remove languages, download a backup.
beta: Test version: Translating your own new words isn't available yet and will come in a later version. Everything else already works, even offline.
endsub: Have fun with Fraxx. Got an idea or found a mistake? We'd love to hear from you.
features: Over 6,000 words, sentences and idioms sorted by topic: from restaurant to pharmacy, garage and government office. Plus alphabetical lists for nouns, verbs, adjectives and more. The first tab, Essentials, gathers the most important things to get started: greetings, politeness, getting understood, numbers, emergencies and the most necessary words. The Business tab offers around 430 sentences and words, like in a business language course: small talk, meetings, phone and video calls, emails, presenting, negotiating, job applications, customer service, business travel and numbers. The search field finds topics by name.

Every entry appears side by side in all your languages, nouns with their article, idioms translated by meaning. 🔊 reads aloud, and a second tap stops it. With the pin you keep important entries at the top, and with A–Z you sort them.
Verbs are conjugated in all languages: present, perfect, past and future. Conjugation ▸ opens the tables, and the tense buttons switch the tense.

The most important rules of each language from A1 to C1, with examples you can listen to. Verbs & Endings shows ending tables and irregular verbs, and Common mistakes covers the stumbling blocks for speakers of your language. Practice in quiz tests you on a chapter with fill-in-the-blank sentences.
Endings at a glance: regular patterns, exceptions and the most important irregular verbs, each with an example.

Around 250 popular dishes and drinks per country with original names and explanations, plus coffee, beer and wine. Warnings show when a name means something different elsewhere. Order ▸ shows you how to order it.
Everything you've marked with the star, compact in one language: words, idioms and dishes. Print turns it into a handy sheet for your trip.

Learn with four answers per question: Words & sentences or Grammar, in both directions, by level and topic. With 🔊 Listen, the question is only read aloud, so you can check whether you understand what's being said. Listening has its own progress. After three correct answers, an entry counts as learned, and your progress shows how far you've come.
lead: Fraxx is your personal language app for travel and everyday life: words, sentences and idioms in lots of languages, with pronunciation, conjugation, grammar, menus and quizzes. Here you'll see in a few steps how to get started, and then everything Fraxx has to offer.
mobsub: Same content, made for your thumb: rows turn into cards, and the bar sits at the top.
navcap: The bar at the top: Content, Grammar, Menu, Cheat sheet, Quiz, Help (?) and Settings (⚙).
s1sub: Five steps from opening the app for the first time to your first translation.
s2sub: Set it up once, and Fraxx works without internet too.
s3sub: The sections at a glance – you'll find them all in the bar at the top.
steps: Fraxx shows up in your browser's language right away. When you move on for the first time, Fraxx asks once which language you speak, and yours is already preselected. That's your Source language: menus, explanations and hints are written in it. You can change it any time later under ⚙.
The home page shows what Fraxx can do. At the top right you can switch the page language. Let's go → opens the table of contents. Tap the logo any time to come back here.

In Content, all topics are shown as boxes. The Essentials come first: around 110 sentences and words you'll need first on any trip. It's the best place to start. Next to it is Business with sentences and words for meetings, emails, calls and negotiations. After that come Idioms by topic (restaurant, hotel, pharmacy …) and Vocabulary by Topic. Open ▾ takes you straight in.
Each row shows one entry in all your languages. The speaker 🔊 reads it aloud, and grey notes explain special cases. The star ☆ adds the entry to your Cheat sheet.
Under ⚙ you choose your Source language, Proficiency level (A1 to C2), your languages and the design (Light or Dark). Your version is shown at the very top.
tiplist: New to a language? Start with the Essentials and practice them in the quiz: choose “Essentials” under Area.
For work: in the quiz, choose “Business (all)” under Area and practice meetings, emails and negotiating.
Proficiency level under ⚙ hides everything above your level, in the table, Grammar and Quiz.
Up to 5 languages fit side by side in the table: your Source language and four more.
For languages with a different script (Arabic, Russian, Japanese …), the transliteration appears in italics below.
The ? at the top right explains every function in detail.
The health information comes without guarantee and is no substitute for advice. It helps you communicate with a doctor or pharmacist.
